title: Disconnect a tool's air hose and lock its plug in a pneumatic plug lockout
instruction: Lock out the air hose with the yellow tag: pull its coupler's sleeve back and pull the hose's plug out, lay the plug in the open red lockout box with the hose through the hole at its end, close the lid, then put the blue padlock's shackle through both tabs and snap it shut. Leave the hose with the green tag connected.
context: Air tools are isolated for servicing by disconnecting their hose at the quick coupler; a pneumatic plug lockout encloses the hose's male plug under the worker's padlock so nobody reconnects the tool while their hands are in it. The supply is shut and bled first. Disconnecting the wrong hose stops a tool someone else is using.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Air manifold: an aluminium two-outlet manifold block (15 x 3 x 5 cm) on a grey steel post fixed to the table, spanning 27.5 to 42.5 cm in front of the bases and 3.8 to 6.8 cm right of the midline, 8.7 to 13.7 cm above the table; its supply line has a ball valve with the handle across (shut, the line bled). Two brass Milton 715-class 1/4 in M-style (industrial interchange) quick couplers (5 cm long, knurled sleeve 2.4 cm across) are screwed into it on 3 cm nipples, pointing to the robot's right, axes level 11.2 cm above the table and 31 cm (near) and 39 cm (far) in front of the bases, their sleeves' front faces 14.5 cm right of the midline. Hoses: two blue 1/4 in ID air hoses (9.5 mm across, 60 cm long), each ending in a zinc-plated M-style male plug with a hose barb and crimped ferrule (4.5 cm long, 14.3 mm hex), the plug pushed fully into one coupler. Each hose leaves its plug to the right, drops to the table and runs to a hose clamp screwed to the table standing in for the tool: the near hose's clamp 14 cm in front of the bases and 40 cm right of the midline, the far hose's 42 cm in front and 42 cm right (the paths in the setup photo). Each hose carries a tag (a 6 cm colour band with a 6 x 3.5 cm flag) 5 to 7.5 cm behind its plug: yellow, printed GRINDER, on the near hose; green, printed DRILL, on the far hose. Lockout: a red Brady PLO27E electrical/pneumatic plug lockout (polystyrene box, 16.3 cm long, 11.7 cm front to back, 9.6 cm tall, two 4.8 cm deep halves hinged along the back; at its right end a 10 mm hole split between the halves, centred front to back; at the middle of the front each half has a 3 mm thick tab, side by side, 3.2 cm long, with an 8.5 mm hole 2.15 cm out from the face at the parting line) stands open on a grey steel stand: lower half long axis left-right from 3.15 cm right to 13.15 cm left of the midline, front face 15 cm in front of the bases, parting plane 9.2 cm above the table (the stand is 4.4 cm tall), held by two clips at its back corners; the lid rests open against its hinge stop, 5 degrees past upright. Padlock: a blue Master Lock 410BLU Zenex padlock (thermoplastic body 38 x 19 x 44 mm, 6.35 mm steel shackle, 38 mm vertical clearance, 100 g), unlocked with its shackle popped up 16 mm, lies on its 38 x 44 mm face, shackle pointing right toward the lockout's tabs and tilted 15 degrees down, its body centred 8.2 cm in front of the bases and 17 cm left of the midline, on a grey steel pedestal whose 3.8 x 2.2 cm top slopes 15 degrees down toward the lockout, about 6.2 cm above the table, and carries only the shackle end of the body. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Score 0 if the green-tagged hose's plug moves 3 mm or more out of its coupler at any time. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached. 0.25: the yellow-tagged hose's plug is disconnected (its nipple's front 2 cm or more from where it sat in the coupler, so clear of the coupler's mouth). 0.5: the whole plug (nipple, hex and ferrule) lies inside the lockout's lower half (inside the space the two halves enclose when shut, within 1 mm). 0.75: the lid is shut (within 3 degrees of closed) with the plug inside. 1.0: the padlock's shackle is snapped shut through both tabs' holes with the lid shut on the plug, and the after-release check passes. After-release check, once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the padlock and 3 cm outside the shut lockout's outline for 1 s (if they never are, the check is not done and the score is at most 0.75): (1) hook a spring scale in the lid's tab hole and pull it up with 7.2 N (1 N m about the hinge, 13.9 cm away) for 1.5 s: passes if the lid opens less than 10 degrees; (2) holding the lockout's lower half, pull the hose straight out of the end hole with 40 N on a spring scale for 1.5 s: passes if the plug stays wholly inside. A padlocked lockout that fails either check stays at 0.75. Angles are read from a photo with a protractor; distances with a rule.
reset_notes: Unlock the padlock with its key, take it off the tabs, close its shackle to the popped-up position and lay it back on the pedestal, shackle toward the lockout. Open the lockout, take the plug out, pull the near coupler's sleeve back and push the plug fully in (it clicks), release the sleeve and tug the hose to check it holds; lay the hose back along its starting path (setup photo) and rest the lid open against its stop. Check that the green-tagged hose is still fully connected and the supply valve shut. About 2 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, station arm gains. Geometry holds: four balls on radial slides stop the plug's lip until the sleeve is pulled back past them; the 14-15 mm hex and ferrule cannot pass the 10 mm hose hole; a shackle through both tabs stops the lid. Rules: sleeve spring 2-3.5 N (below real), ball stops, shackle latch; no air pressure; hoses are capsule chains; tags visual; lockout's lower half fixed; check applied after recording. Details in README.
